title: The Chinese Labour Corps on the Western Front
summary: Some 140,000 Chinese men worked for the British and French in the First World War, unloading ships, digging trenches, repairing roads and railways and later clearing mines.
why: Kept the Allied supply lines running in the First World War.

unsung.contribution: Provided the labour that built depots, trenches, roads and railways behind Allied lines.
unsung.recognition: Their contribution went largely uncommemorated for decades and was later 'airbrushed from history'; they were ineligible for the Military Medal.
